Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Nexara Cloud Technologies Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to request through the phone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jennings, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jennings:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing Nexara Cloud Technologies' results for the third quarter of fiscal 2024. With me on the call are Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Marcus Hale, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Liam Chen, Chief Technology Officer; Sophia Reyes, Chief Product Officer; Dylan Ortiz, Chief Marketing Officer; Nora Fisk, Chief Sales Officer; and Theo Grant, Chief Security Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Nexara Cloud Technologies continued its strong growth trajectory in the third quarter, driven by robust demand for our comprehensive suite of cloud services and solutions.

During the quarter, our key priorities included:
1. Expanding our presence in emerging markets.
2. Accelerating the adoption of our AI-powered platform.
3. Enhancing our developer ecosystem.
4. Strengthening our commitment to sustainability.
5. Investing in employee training and development.
6. Improving cross-functional collaboration.
7. Ensuring the security and privacy of our customers' data.

I'm particularly excited about our enterprise customer wins and the momentum in large deals this quarter, which really highlight our position as the preferred platform for mission-critical workloads. We secured $1.2 billion in total enterprise annual contract value, up 45% year-over-year, accounting for 62% of our overall bookings. This included 28 deals over $10 million in total contract value—a quarterly record—and six mega-deals surpassing $100 million.

Standouts include GlobalBank, a top-5 U.S. financial institution, which expanded with a $250 million, five-year commitment building on their existing $150 million footprint in our Nexara AI Data Lakehouse. This extends to real-time fraud detection using our GenAI Vector Engine with NVIDIA H100 GPUs, migrating 2.5 petabytes of on-prem Hadoop to our serverless compute for 40% TCO savings, adding $85 million in net new ARR.

In healthcare, the EuroHealth Consortium—covering 12 major EU hospitals—signed a $180 million multi-region sovereign cloud deal using our compliant Nexara Sovereign Zones with FIPS 140-3 encryption and zero-trust setup for federated learning in personalized medicine on our Kubernetes-native platform, boosting our EMEA healthcare share by 25% amid GDPR pressures.

InnoTech, a major SaaS provider, expanded for $120 million on our Nexara Edge Cloud Fabric, powering IoT analytics at 500+ edge sites with 65% latency cuts via 5G-optimized WASM runtimes integrated with their AI stack—a land-and-expand from a $5 million pilot to 8x net retention.

Regionally, Americas led with 55% of ACV at $660 million from financial services and retail SAP S/4HANA migrations via Rise with Nexara. EMEA added 28% or $336 million in DACH manufacturing and UK public sector. APAC grew 70% YoY to $204 million with Japanese telco 6G orchestration and Australian mining sustainability plays.

AI drove 68% of large deals via Nexara GenAI Studio for Llama 3.1 fine-tuning at 10 petaFLOPS, with 3x inference surge and 72% hybrid multi-cloud wins. Enterprise net retention hit 128%, expansion revenue $450 million, pipeline $18 billion up 52% YoY, with 65% weighted to Q4. RFPs for AI sovereignty up 40% in EMEA, U.S. DoD deals accelerating post-CMMC Level 3. These wins showcase our hyperscale economics and resilience, powering cloud-native transformation.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Marcus Hale to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Marcus Hale:
Thank you, Elena. We are pleased to report another quarter of strong financial results. Revenue grew by 16.5% year-over-year to $28.4 billion, exceeding our guidance. Our gross margin was 72.8%, reflecting our efficient cost structure. Our operating margin was 28.5%.

A key factor shaping our top-line this quarter was foreign exchange fluctuations. As a global hyperscaler with over 45% of revenue from outside the U.S., our usage-based IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS model exposes us to currency volatility, with billing in local currencies like the euro, yen, GBP, and Brazilian real.

FX headwinds reduced reported revenue growth by $425 million, or 1.5 points. Constant currency growth was 18% YoY. This is the third straight quarter of negative impact from the dollar's 7% strengthening against key currencies, similar to AWS and Azure's 1-2% drags.

Regionally: EMEA (28% of revenue) saw $210 million hit, 3.2% headwind from euro's 6% drop amid ECB cuts and 0.3% GDP; constant currency ARR $12.5 billion up 22% from sovereign cloud in Frankfurt/Paris. APAC (12%) $115 million adverse, 2.8% drag from yen -4.5%, AUD -3%; constant currency +25%, AI training up 40% YoY in Tokyo/Sydney with NVIDIA H100s, India SMB +30%. LATAM/Other (5%) $100 million headwind from real -5%; constant currency +28% from edge in São Paulo/Mexico City.

TTM FX impact $1.2 billion, 70 bps drag, up from $400 million last year.

Mitigations: Hedging covers 65-75% of 12-month exposures, Q3 gains $180 million offsetting 42%; targeting 70% into FY2025. 80% local currency billing (up from 65% two years ago), dynamic pricing in Nexara Console for real-time FX adjustments, NRR 112%. Capex acceleration to local regions, $2.5 billion FY2024 including $800 million for SE Asia/Middle East AZs, 35% RPO growth, 50% AI/ML inference.

Q4 FX 1-2% headwind at current rates; guidance Q4 $29.0-29.5 billion constant currency 19-20%, FY2024 $115-118 billion. Diversified mix—55% enterprise, 25% AI—plus usage elasticity amid 22% cloud CAGR per Gartner positions us strongly.

Next, I'd like to introduce Dr. Liam Chen, who will provide an update on our technology roadmap.

Dr. Liam Chen:
Thank you, Marcus. We are making significant investments in research and development to stay at the forefront of cloud innovation. We are particularly excited about our progress in AI/ML infrastructure.

Our Cloud Services segment hit $25.6 billion in Q3, up 18% quarter-over-quarter from $21.7 billion and 28% YoY from $20.0 billion, outpacing IDC's 22% IaaS/PaaS growth.

By category: Compute/Storage (52%) $13.3 billion, +22% QoQ/32% YoY from Nexara Compute Graviton4 instances (30% better price/performance), streaming migrations, Nexara Object Storage +25% with Iceberg data lakes. AI/ML/Analytics (28%) $7.2 billion, +35% QoQ/52% YoY—inference on Nexara SageMaker-like foundation models +60% QoQ, agentic AI, RPO $18 billion +45%, NVIDIA H100/Blackwell partnerships capturing 15% more training. Database/Networking/Developer Tools (15%) $3.8 billion, +12% QoQ/20% YoY—Aurora Serverless v3, Global Accelerator latency -25%. Other (5%) $1.3 billion +15% incl. Nexara GuardDuty.

Ex-FX (2 pts), YoY 30%; NRR 128% +200 bps QoQ, top 1,000 +35% YoY.

Regions: Americas (55%) $14.1 billion +17% QoQ/26% YoY from enterprise SAP migrations. EMEA (25%) $6.4 billion +20%/30% sovereign in Germany/UK. APAC (20%) $5.1 billion +22%/35% Japan/India 5G/digital sovereignty, capacity adds in Tokyo/Mumbai.

Investments: 1M+ new Graviton instances, 25-40% TCO cuts for inference; Nexara EKS with Karpenter. GA Nexara AI Studio no-code fine-tuning, 5,000 adopters; 100% renewable matching. Multi-cloud Outposts, usage economics; RPO $112 billion +42% YoY, 85% 12-month deployable. Capacity ahead via $12B YTD capex; Q4 guide $27.2-27.8 billion, 20-22% YoY.

Now, I'll pass it to Sophia Reyes for a product update.

Sophia Reyes:
Thank you, Dr. Chen. We recently launched Nexara Fabric 2.0, which is already gaining significant traction in the market.

Our overall gross margin reached 72.8%, up 220 basis points YoY and 110 sequentially—11th straight expansion quarter, T4Q avg 72.1% above peer 68%.

Mix shift: IaaS (compute/storage) 28% YoY to 43% revenue, 65.4% margins; PaaS (Nexara Kube/serverless) +42% to 35%, 78.2%; SaaS/AI (Nexara AI Studio/vector DBs) +68% to 22%, 85.6%—140 bps from mix.

Tailwinds: 48 regions, 2.5M servers at 92% util (+4%); Graviton3 across 70% fleet -25% power/core, -20% customer TCO, dep/amort -15% QoQ; AI 18% compute hours, 82% margins. Renewables 65% (80% FY25 target), liquid cooling PUE sub-1.15; bandwidth -8% rev%.

Headwinds: $4.2B capex dep 50 bps; pricing matches 30 bps; labor +5%.

Regions: NA 52% rev 74.2% AI density; EMEA 71.5% +300 bps sovereign Paris online; APAC 28% rev 70.8% expansions; LATAM 68.9% improving.

Ahead: Q4 73.0-73.5%, FY24 72.5%; Nexara Fabric SDN +10% eff; AI 25% rev FY25 84%+; $10B edge 5G; PPAs nuclear SMRs, quantum-safe.

This flywheel of scale, innovation outpaces peers on profitability for GenAI opportunity.

I'll now hand it over to Dylan Ortiz to discuss our marketing strategy.

Dylan Ortiz:
Thank you, Sophia. Our marketing efforts are focused on building brand awareness and generating demand for our solutions.

Pricing strategies and discounting were pivotal to our 28% revenue growth to $8.2 billion, cloud services $7.5 billion (92%). Pricing added 15 points, but non-GAAP gross margin dipped 120 bps to 74.2%.

Models: On-demand 35% ($2.6B +45% YoY) 82% margins, AI GPUs spot 85-90% off. RCIs/Savings Plans 55% ($4.1B +35%) 72% margins, $1.2B expansions, $500M EU automaker. Spot/promo 10% ($800M +60%) 55-60%, 92% util AutoScaler.

Discount avg 28% (+4 pts, below AWS 30-35%): Competitive 10-20% for migrations, 240 enterprise incl. 40% Azure displacement, $450M ARR. Volume/bundle 15% StratoS3 >1PB +52% to $1.1B, AI suite 25%. AI Accelerate promo waived egress, 35% trial conversion, 12K devs $150M pipeline.

Customers +31% to 2.8M, NRR 118%, ARPU -4% $92. Regions: NA 55% $4.1B low disc 22%; EMEA 25% $1.9B 25% sovereign premiums; APAC 15% $1.1B 35%; LATAM 5% $400M 30% edge.

Tech: DPE 2.0 ML pricing -8% over-disc $120M save; sustainability 7% green off. Target 76% margins: upsells 40%, AI tiers, 75% promo retention. Pricing 12-14 pts FY24 growth, disc 27%; capex eff 40% custom silicon pricing power.

Stickiness proven.

Next, I'd like to introduce Nora Fisk, who will provide an update on our sales performance.

Nora Fisk:
Thank you, Dylan. Our sales team delivered a strong performance in the third quarter, driven by increased customer adoption of our cloud services.

On data center expansion and capex: Q3 $3.2B, H1 $6.1B +28% YoY for $28.5B RPO (42% AI +2x YoY). FY24 $12.5-14B (18-20% rev intensity): 65% P&E, 25% servers/GPUs, rest network/edge.

2.2 GW new capacity 12 regions, total 8 GW end-year (12 GW FY25). Americas 55% 1.2 GW: 500 MW N. Virginia/Phoenix H100/Blackwell 120 kW/rack, 1.5 GW power to 2027, 80% renewable PUE <1.15 liquid cooling. EMEA 25% 300 MW Frankfurt sovereign ARM, 200 MW Milan 5G PUE 1.05 immersion. APAC 20% 500 MW Mumbai (Reliance), Tokyo modular, Sydney sovereign, Nitro accelerators 25% TCO.

Supply: GPU 4-6 mo lead, 15% PODs 9 mo deploy. Power pipeline 4 GW vs. 1,000 TWh 2026 demand. Q4 $3.5-3.8B 800 MW, AI 70%; FY26 stabilize 15-17% rev, FCF >25%, 2-3x ROI 24 mo.

Supports raised FY24 rev $72-74B.

Finally, I'll pass it to Theo Grant to discuss our security initiatives.

Theo Grant:
Thank you, Nora. Security is our top priority. We are committed to protecting our customers' data and maintaining the highest standards of security.

Our data breach prevention and incident response are key differentiators, boosting enterprise win rates 28% YoY via SecureVault zero-trust. Breaches cost $4.88M avg; we've invested $1.2B security R&D (12% capex > Gartner 8-10%).

Prevention: Defense-in-depth NIST/Zero Trust across 25 regions. Sentinel AI 99.7% anomaly accuracy on 15PB telemetry, blocked 2.47M attacks Q3 (340K zero-days) -42% YoY, $150M savings. AES-256 KMS quantum-resistant, TLS 1.3 PFS, MFA +35% uptake -62% compromise. Falco/Trivy scanned 1.2B containers, 18K vulns 89% auto-remediate.

Regions: EMEA GDPR/NIS2 zero incidents +25% retention; APAC ML vs. APT41 +55%; Americas HIPAA/FedRAMP $2.8B pipeline. SecureVault +15-20% pricing, $450M Q3 ARR +32%.

Response: GIRT 350 experts MTTD 4.2 min (-67%), MTTR 27 min top 5% Forrester. 95% SOAR auto Splunk/XSOAR/IR-Orchestrator, 1,200 incidents 87% <1hr contained. Chaos drills MITRE 98/100, CrowdStrike co-dev. Recover 99.999% 4hr immutable backups; sim APJ 19 min zero exfil.

Insurance flat 0.4% rev save $28M. Ahead: $450M FY25 homomorphic/blockchain quantum; stack 22% lower TCO, zero security churn finance 15% $18.2B ARR. Moat for 25%+ EBITDA.

Back to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, everyone. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Operator:
Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Elena, can you elaborate on the FX headwinds and how your hedging and local billing are mitigating ongoing dollar strength into next year?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Emily. As Marcus detailed, FX shaved 1.5 points this quarter, but our layered hedging offset 42%, and 80% local billing plus dynamic pricing kept NRR solid at 112%. We're targeting 70% hedge coverage into FY2025, and regional investments reduce translation risk. With underlying demand resilient, we're guiding constant currency growth comfortably.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel:
Great, thanks. Marcus, on gross margins at 72.8%—impressive expansion. What are the biggest drivers looking into Q4, and any concerns from capex or pricing pressures?

Marcus Hale:
Appreciate it, Raj. Mix shift to high-margin PaaS/AI at 85%+ contributed 140 bps, plus scale at 92% utilization and Graviton efficiencies. Headwinds like dep from $4.2B capex were 50 bps, but renewables and SDN keep us on track for 73-73.5% Q4. Pricing discipline ensures we balance growth and profitability.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong:
Thanks. Theo or Liam, with cyber threats rising, how are your prevention measures impacting costs, and any incidents to note this quarter?

Dr. Liam Chen:
Thanks, Lisa. Theo covered our robust setup—no escalations to breaches, Sentinel AI blocked 2.47M attacks with $150M savings. Investments are 12% capex but revenue-positive via SecureVault premiums and top retention. Costs controlled, insurance flat, positioning us for the $103B security market growth.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you for your questions. We appreciate your continued support.

Sarah Jennings:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
